headline: A proposed data center campus drew public comment, and a special town meeting was scheduled on a petition to bar data centers.
summary: A speaker said the proposed campus would have 10 buildings and 900 megawatts, on over 440 acres bought from the Kraft Group. Other speakers raised concerns about well water, noise, and traffic, and one asked for an independent review. A special town meeting on a citizen petition to bar data centers was scheduled for January 4. The budget preview projected a deficit of about $300,000 for FY 2028, rising to about $8.3 million by FY 2033.
decisions: Approved 5-0 a Class II used-car license for Mas Garage LLC at 99 Worcester-Providence Turnpike, limited to 16 unregistered cars and 10 registered repair vehicles, expiring January 1st, 2028.
Approved 5-0 scheduling a special town meeting for January 4 at 7:00 p.m. in the Ramshorn gym.
discussion: Data center proposal: Public speakers opposed the 10-building, 900-megawatt campus over well water, noise, and traffic, and asked for an independent review and a final vote by town meeting. Other speakers urged a careful, fact-based review of the possible commercial tax base.

FY 2028 budget preview: The budget presentation projected a deficit of about $300,000 for FY 2028, and members asked how health insurance costs are split between the town and the schools. Members also asked for the forecast assumptions to be published.

Used-car license limits: Members debated how to count unregistered and repair vehicles, and who would enforce the limit, likely the building commissioner. Members leaned toward the commissioner's recommendation of 16 for sale and 10 for repair, and a speaker opposed another car dealership on Route 146.

Special town meeting timing: Members chose January 4 over January 2, since most people would be back from the holiday break. Electronic voting clickers were proposed for the meeting, with up to about 2,500 available.
